newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols softer after post-data bounce.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols softer after post-data bounce.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options softened as the underlying bond market rebounded after a sharp drop early in the session on stronger-than-expected June retail sales data, dealers said.

They said the market had pumped risk-premium into option prices at the opening ahead of the numbers, regarded as the most important data this week, but quickly stripped it out as the bonds' decline proved short-lived.
"Shortly after the number, after we bounced back up, it came back to where it was yesterday," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Implied volatility for at-the-money September T-bond futures options stood at around 8.0 percent in late trade, down from about 8.4 at the open and 8.2 at Monday's close.
"They got hit after the numbers and they've been down ever since," a second CBOT brokerage trader said.
Talk in the market was selling by a big commercial firm of about 2,000 contracts each in September 113 puts, 112 puts and 111 puts.
"They're really smacking vols there," the first trader said.
"Also, that had the effect of taming the skew a little bit," he added, referring to the richness in volatility levels of out-of-the-money puts relative to those of equivalent out-of-the-money calls.
Traders expected little stimulus from Wednesday's consumer price index (CPI), given continued no-inflation signal in last Friday's producer price index.
In addition, Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony is not due until next week, pressuring volatilities for August options, which expire on Friday.
Still, a bank was said to have bought 2,000 contracts of the August 115 calls.
"People are pretty much taking lottery picks," the brokerage trader said.
Short-dated options have high gamma, which provides quick premium acceleration, but are vulnerable to time decay.
The August 115 calls have delta of only 11, and a quick rally in bonds is needed for gamma to start working in favor of the holder.
In Eurodollar options, volatilities were steady to marginally firmer.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options were up 0.1 point at 9.4 percent, while the March volatility rose 0.2 point to 11.2 percent.
Traders said volatility levels had become so low that market-makers were unwilling to lower volatilities further ahead of the Humphrey Hawkins testimony.
